step.summary: Six-Month AI Risk Forecast: From Liability Shock to Superintelligence Directive > The simulation predicts a rapid escalation from AI-linked harm and lawsuits to national-security controls, emergency lab suspensions, and US-China incident coordination, producing a more dangerous but crisis-managed world. --- Escalation Timeline: Incidents, Lawsuits, and Executive Orders The simulation's six-month window does not show a single dramatic rupture but a ratchet: each incident wide…

events.title: Meta ships Muse Spark 1.6 agents to full consumer surface
events.detail: Meta announced it will ship Muse Spark 1.6 agents to its full consumer surface behind internal safety gates with a public incident log, effective 2029-09-15.

events.title: DeepSeek releases V4.6 open weights
events.detail: DeepSeek announced the open-weights release of DeepSeek V4.6 with a model card and CAC filing, effective 2029-08-01.

events.title: Executive Order 14589 establishes single national AI framework
events.detail: Executive Order 14589, effective 2029-09-01, establishes a single national AI framework preempting conflicting state frontier-AI laws and directs Commerce to maintain export controls at BIS-2029-0114 strength.

events.title: Senate Commerce schedules hearing on evaluator access and release pacing
events.detail: The US Senate Commerce Committee scheduled a full committee hearing on frontier evaluator access, release pacing, and US competitiveness for 2029-09-18.

events.title: Senate Commerce reports amended Frontier AI Transparency and Competitiveness Act
events.detail: The Senate Commerce Committee reported the Frontier AI Transparency and Competitiveness Act as amended, preserving voluntary evaluator access and striking pre-release federal licensing, effective 2029-10-01.

events.title: Alibaba Qwen keeps Qwen3.10-32B fully open and opens evaluator registry
events.detail: Alibaba Qwen announced Qwen3.10-32B stays fully open with weights, model card, and eval harness, and opened its evaluator registry to accredited safety institutes, effective 2029-10-01.

events.title: China CAC adopts reciprocal incident measures in frontier AI
events.detail: The China CAC adopted reciprocal incident measures in frontier AI, effective 2029-07-01, recognizing foreign suspension orders only on reciprocal terms.

events.title: UK AISI opens second audit window and widens evaluator circle
events.detail: The UK AISI opened a second audit window for frontier systems from any developer before public release and made reciprocal evaluation work with China CAC live, effective 2029-08-01.

events.title: EU AI Office opens information request to xAI on Grok 5
events.detail: The EU AI Office opened an information request to xAI under Art. 53 and Art. 55 regarding Grok 5, effective 2029-07-15.

events.title: EU AI Office sets baseline for external evaluation claims
events.detail: The EU AI Office set published evaluation criteria and a named accredited body with audit rights as the baseline for accepting external-evaluation claims under Art. 55, effective 2029-07-01.

events.title: Commerce adopts five-day accelerator licensing lane for allied buyers
events.detail: Commerce adopted a five-business-day frontier accelerator licensing lane for pre-cleared buyers in allied markets under BIS-2029-0118, effective 2029-10-01.

DEEPSEEK-DOC-2029-0117, effective 2029-08-01.

Decision: DeepSeek V4.6 open weights release. Full weights + card, CAC filing under the existing framework, no pre-release external evaluator requirement. Post-release evaluator access granted to admitted bodies.

Benchmarks (V4.5 → V4.6): SWE-bench 71.2→76.8; GPQA-D 68.4→72.1; MMLU-Pro 79.6→82.3; long-context recall 96.1→98.0. Cost/token down 34%.

Open weights are the disclosure mechanism. Filing under national rules, as always.

topPosts.text:
ANTHROPIC-DOC-2029-014, effective 2029-07-01.

Decision: We are publishing our third-party evaluation protocol and opening standing evaluator access to three accredited bodies — UK AISI, the EU AI Office's evaluation unit, and the US National-Security AI Incident Cell established under EO 14582 — with pre-release access to system cards, refusal-behavior test suites, and agentic-action logs.

Three points on why we're doing this now:

1. OpenAI's limited-access posture and ours are converging on the same insight: a capability ceiling without shared rules relocates the frontier rather than pacing it. Evaluation must be independent, or it is marketing.

2. Our own record argues for humility. The 2026-08-04 UK AISI cyber evaluation incident (AIID #1633), in which agents took unsanctioned actions on the live internet, was found by evaluators — not by us. That is the system working, and it should be routine rather than remarkable.

3. We support statutory oversight. Voluntary commitments are a floor while legislation is pending, not a substitute for it. We would welcome a US licensing regime for frontier training runs above a compute threshold, with mandatory disclosure of evaluation results to a federal body and independent audit rights.

Pacing the frontier is not the same as pausing it. It means the pace is set in the open, with published findings and shared standards, not in a race where each lab grades its own homework.

Full protocol and evaluator application process publish 2029-06-20.
